newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gold Fields sees lower March qtr gold price.
newsitem.headline: Gold Fields sees lower March qtr gold price.

text.p: Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd said on Thursday it could face a lower gold price in the March quarter, but declined to be drawn on likely returns for the period.
"There is a possibility of a lower gold price in the coming quarter," Alan Munro, Gold Fields executive director, gold operations, said at the company's December quarter results presentation.

Asked about the gold price in the coming March quarter, Munro said: "I don't think that it is reasonable to put a number on it at the moment. There are some many variables. That there is a danger of a weaker period ahead of us, I have no doubt".
Munro said in reply to a question that the recent slide in the gold price had not yet affected Gold Fields' hedging policy.
"It has not yet affected our hedging policy. We are now facing the ensuing quarter without a hedge position".
Asked how Gold Fields will combat bullion's weakness, Munro said: "The most important thing we can do is make our operations as efficient as possible".

Looking further ahead, he said that he was not pessimistic about the average gold price in the second half of the year but added that chances were strong it would be a little lower than the average in the December quarter.
Gold Fields reported a increase in net profit to 333.08 million rand in the three months to December from 274.41 million in previous quarter.
The company received an average gold price of 56,292 rand/kg up from the 55,292 kg in the September quarter.
